Cc: cto@acme-payments.com

Subject: Production latency and 5xx spikes — Acme reserved capacity

Hi Logan / Redwood ops,

We're seeing sustained P95 latency climb from ~120ms to 1.8s across the auth and payment-authorization routes starting at ~07:55 PST and a 5xx wave on the payments model. Token throttles and queueing are triggering fallback logic on our side which is impacting customer checkouts. Our observability team attached a short window of traces and error logs (attached acme_latency_log_2026-12-01.txt).

We are on reserved capacity and have a committed SLA. This is impacting live transactions — we need immediate remediation and a concrete ETA on when throughput will normalize. If there's an ops or exec channel, please escalate.

Thanks,
Sally Vargas
Head of Platform Reliability
Acme Payments

Subject: RE: Production latency and 5xx spikes — Acme reserved capacity

Quick diagnostic from the stack: we’re observing a queue-depth increase on the dedicated GPU pool servicing Acme's reservation and a correlated rise in GPU utilization on nodes pinned to their shard. Early signs point to a combination of (a) a sudden traffic surge from Acme (longer sequences from a new feature) and (b) noisy background jobs in the same pool from a different tenant that bypassed soft capping. Result: effective reserved throughput has fallen below the committed QPS for a ~30min window.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (actionable now):
- Enable per-tenant request shaping (already staged, can flip in 5–10m).
- Evict non-reserved background workloads from the Acme shard (10–20m).
- Authorize a temporary burst window (60m) from the burst pool to cover peak demand — requires exec approval.
- Toggle aggressive KV cache warmup for Acme's model to reduce repeated generation costs (hotfix deploy, ~30–45m).

I’ve attached the temporary burst runbook (runbook_temp_burst_policy.pdf) — we should pull legal on credits if we authorize this. If we proceed with burst, ops will need a 1-click approval from leadership.

— Priyom
Principal Systems Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-01T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Production latency and 5xx spikes — Acme reserved capacity

Summary of deep-dive so far: the scheduler’s tenant isolation signal misclassified a subset of long-sequence Acme requests as "best-effort" due to a parsing regression introduced in the latest routing rule set (deployed 11:42 PST). That regression combined with a coincident noisy neighbor increased tail latency and forced some requests into fallback causing the 5xx surface.

Planned fixes / timeline:
- Roll back the routing rule change (target: 15m).
- Force-allocate cache priming for Acme models (target: 30m after rollback).
- If rollback does not normalize, we will proactively migrate Acme to an adjacent reserved shard (target: 60m) and enable burst allocation while migration completes.

We estimate normalization for core request latency within 45–60 minutes if we can approve the rollback and the short burst. I’ll start the rollback now and report back at +15m. Attached are the relevant scheduler logs excerpted from 07:45–08:10 PST.

— David
Director, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

Sally — thanks for your patience. Quick update and commitments from Redwood: 1) we completed a rollback of the routing rule at 11:38 PST and primed the KV cache for your tenant; 2) we authorized a 60-minute temporary burst while we validate the migration plan; 3) ops evicted best-effort background jobs from the shard. Early telemetry shows P95 falling back toward baseline (tracking).

To make this right: we’re offering Acme a one-time 10% service credit for the impacted hour and scheduling a postmortem with your engineering team tomorrow at 10:00am PST to review root cause and permanent safeguards. We’ve also scheduled an exec bridge for 12:30pm PST today (Logan to share dial in) to walk through the timeline and approvals for longer-term changes (per-tenant hard caps, scheduler fixes).

If you prefer, we can extend the temporary burst while migration completes — we’ll need a quick ack to proceed.

Apologies again for the impact — we’ll keep you closely updated.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
